To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a global kinetic analysis of an autocatalyctic zymogen activation mechanism in which the proteinase activity is inhibited.

the kinetic analysis of an inhibition mechanism of an autocatalyic activation process allows to predict the steady state of this process, and that the inhibition mechanism is able to regulate the activation of the process.
the inhibition route prevails in all cases in which the inhibitor is present at a concentration that is at least 10% of that of the zymogen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a model of a zymogen activation process in which the proteinase is inhibited by a reversible inhibitor.
the analysis of the kinetic behaviour of a mechanism of autocatalytic activation of a zymogen in which an inhibitor is present, which competes with the substrate for the enzyme's active site.
the analysis of the kinetic behaviour of a system in which the inhibition of the activation process plays an important role in the regulation of the enzyme activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kinetic behaviour of an autocatalytically activated system can be predicted from the kinetic constants of the system and the concentration of the inhibitor.
the inhibition route is the most important in the steady state, but that the activation route is predominant in the transient phase of the system.
, when the inhibitor concentration is high enough, the system behaves in a way which is very similar to the behaviour of an enzyme-inhibitor system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kinetic analysis of the system studied allows us to predict, under certain conditions, that the inhibition process is predominant over the activation process in the steady state.

we have derived the equations that describe the behaviour of the system in all the possible cases, and that we have introduced a parameter that allows us to predict the steady-state behaviour of the system.

we have derived a new parameter which allows us to know whether the inhibition route is more important than the activation route in a system in which the zymogen activation and inhibition compete for the active site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of an inhibitor, the system can be regulated by the inhibitor concentration.
the steady-state concentration of the proteinase can be controlled by changing the concentrations of the zymogen, the inhibitor or both of them.
the inhibition route is more efficient than the activation route in the steady state when the inhibitor is a competitive inhibitor.
